subject: Urgent: Acme Robotics - burstback 5xxs from KV cache priority inversion
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@acmerobotics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx and throughput collapse - urgent

Jonas,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors around 07:55 PT this morning and a correlated drop in throughput for our model endpoints. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 7% and many inference requests are timing out. Latency P95 has moved from ~120ms to 1.2s. Attached are the last 10k request logs and a short sample of the error lines.

Sample from our logs:
[2029-05-03T07:56:03Z] request_id=acm-8f3a srv=redwood-eu-1 route=/v1/generate status=502 kv_err=priority_inversion lane=small_batch
[2029-05-03T07:56:04Z] request_id=acm-8f3b srv=redwood-eu-1 route=/v1/generate status=504 timeout=token_write

This is affecting our checkout flow; we need an urgent triage and estimated time to restore. We are on an enterprise contract and this is customer-impacting. Can you triage and escalate to your SRE team?

Attached: acme_20290503_app_logs.txt

—
Elena Park
Head of Platform, Acme Robotics
elena@acmerobotics.com

Thanks for the heads up, Elena — sending to SRE immediately.

Naomi / Ben — Acme is seeing a sudden 5xx surge + large P95 increases starting 07:55 PT. Logs attached by the customer show kv_err=priority_inversion and lane=small_batch in the 502s. Please confirm receipt and initial triage ETA. I've attached the logs Elena sent.

Elena — can you confirm if you changed any traffic shaping or routing rules on your side in the last 24 hours? Also paste a couple of affected request_ids if you have them (we'll correlate traces).

—
Jonas Weber

jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and throughput collapse - urgent

Acknowledged — we're triaging. Reproduced the spike on our ingestion metrics. Early indicators point to a priority inversion between the small_token batch lane and the hotkey protection policy: a recent routing tweak (deployed 2029-05-02 22:40 PT) appears to have increased preference for small_token batching on certain tenants, which is starving the KV cache hot-path and causing HOL blocking and cascading token-write timeouts.

Immediate asks:
- Jonas / Ben: please provide two affected request_ids from Elena so we can pull traces.
- Ops: I'm requesting a KV config snapshot and recent routing policy diffs — attaching our runbook and a demand script.

Proposed immediate mitigation (low blast):
1) Temporarily reduce the small_token batch priority for Acme to the prior profile (rollback routing tweak for tenant).
2) Increase per-tenant hotkey protection threshold for the next 30 minutes.
3) Enable KV cache prefetch backoff and increase its TTL for hot prefixes.

I'm preparing a hotfix patch to abort priority inversion when prefetch backlog > 2000 entries. Attaching kv_config_snapshot.json and runbook excerpt.

Attachments referenced: kv_config_snapshot.json; runbook_kv_prioritization.pdf

—
Naomi Feldman
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Jonas — please coordinate the rollback authorization with Acme (they need to approve a tenant-level routing rollback). I'll also open an incident bridge and keep Acme updated every 30 minutes until recovery.

ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmerobotics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Update: root cause and mitigations applied

Status update — root cause identified and mitigations applied.

Summary:
- RCA: a routing change on 2029-05-02 that increased small_token batching preference for Acme caused a sustained influx of small-batch requests which preempted the KV cache hot-path. This triggered priority inversion: small-batch lanes held locks waiting on KV prefetches while large/real-time lanes (including checkout flows) were starved, creating HOL blocking and token-write timeouts (manifested as 502/504).
- Evidence: correlated traces for request_ids acm-8f3a and acm-8f3b show long token_write durations and prefetch backlog > 2300. Kernel-side metrics show spike in cache eviction churn during 07:55-08:10 PT.

Actions taken (12:15–12:40 PT):
1) Rolled back the small_token batching priority for Acme to the previous profile (rollback id: rb-20290503-acme-01).
2) Applied a temporary hotkey protection increase for Acme (hotkey threshold +3000 requests/min) for 1 hour.
3) Deployed patch patch_hotfix_502.patch that aborts prefetch when backlog > 2000 and forces a fast-path for writes.
4) Disabled tenant-level aggressive prefetch for affected prefixes.

Impact: error rate reduced from 7% -> 0.6% within ~12 minutes of mitigations. Throughput returned to ~95% baseline. Monitoring is green but we will keep 1:1 ops watch for 2 hours.

Next steps:
- Follow-up postmortem with config diffs and a long-term fix to avoid priority inversion (owner: Naomi, due 2029-05-06).
- Work with Product to add an automated prefetch backoff when per-tenant backlog passes threshold (owner: Product SRE; timeline: 2 weeks).
- Account team to confirm acceptance with Acme and update the escrowed config.

Elena — please confirm if you saw recovery on your side. If you have more logs for the 08:00–08:20 window, please attach them to the incident ticket (SERV-2029).

Attachments: patch_hotfix_502.patch

—
Naomi Feldman
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
